newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends stronger on bullish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends stronger on bullish sentiment.

text.p: The won closed higher versus the dollar on Monday buoyed by generally bullish sentiment towards the local currency and a weaker dollar against the Japanese yen in world markets, traders said.
The won closed at 893.00, compared with Friday's close of 894.10. It traded in a range of 892.60 to 894.20.
Expected month-end export deals and a rise in inflow of foreign funds for equity investment following the scheduled foreign stock ownership expansion on May 2 fuelled the sentiment, they said.
The foreign stock holding limit will be raised to 23 percent from the current 20 percent.
"A new direction for the dollar would be set after early May," said a local dealer. "But until then the dollar is likely to trade in a narrow range."
Traders forecast the won to move in a range of 892 and 894 on Tuesday.
Tuesday's mid-rate is seen pegged at 893.10 against 893.70 today.
